name: GE Aerospace
legalName: General Electric Company (operates as GE Aerospace)
description: GE Aerospace makes and services jet engines. Its installed base is about 50,000 commercial and 30,000 military engines, and the aftermarket (spare parts, overhauls and service agreements on engines already flying) is about 70% of revenue per the 10-K. It sells new engines, including the LEAP, largely through the CFM International joint venture with Safran (a non-consolidated equity investment), at thin or even negative margin, then earns years of high-margin service on each engine. Commercial Engines & Services is 73% of revenue; Defense & Propulsion is the rest. Corporate also carries a run-off insurance business ($3.5B of 2025 revenue, from legacy GE) that is in the revenue total but is not aerospace. Revenue is booked mostly to airlines, airframers (Boeing, Airbus), third-party overhaul shops and governments.

gics.note: Conventional GICS label from general knowledge; not re-checked against MSCI/S&P. SEC SIC 3600 (Electronic & Other Electrical Equipment), a legacy code from the old conglomerate.

hq.note: 1 Neumann Way, Evendale, OH 45215 (FY2025 10-K cover); also offices in Washington DC and Norwalk, Connecticut

employees.note: About 57,000 people, about 30,000 in the US (FY2025 10-K)

businessLines.name: Commercial Engines & Services (CES)
businessLines.how: Sells engines to airframers and airlines, then earns recurring spare-parts and shop-visit revenue over decades of service; services were $25,010M of $33,314M (75%) in 2025. Internal shop visit revenue grew 24%.
businessLines.description: Jet engines for commercial airframes, business aviation and aeroderivative applications, plus services: overhaul (MRO), spare parts, long-term service agreements.

operatingProfit.note: segment profit as reported (before Corporate & Other costs of $568M and eliminations of $534M, as defined in the 10-K); share computed against the $10,157M sum of the two segments

businessLines.name: Defense & Propulsion Technologies (DPT)
businessLines.how: Sells engines and systems to governments and primes on multi-year contracts, then services; driven by government funding. Defense & Systems $6,574M and Propulsion & Additive Technologies $3,980M.
businessLines.description: Military engines (e.g. F110), defense systems and Propulsion & Additive Technologies (Avio Aero, aircraft systems).

operatingProfit.note: segment profit as reported (before Corporate & Other costs of $568M and eliminations of $534M, as defined in the 10-K); share computed against the $10,157M sum of the two segments

businessLines.name: Corporate & Other (mainly run-off insurance)
businessLines.how: Insurance premiums and investment income from a legacy book; not a growth business.
businessLines.description: Legacy insurance run-off operations, plus intersegment eliminations.

brands.name: CFM International (LEAP, CFM56)
brands.note: 50-50 joint venture with Safran; equity method, related-party transactions with GE

whatsNext.text: Reporting change: CES expands to the full engine lifecycle and the aeroderivative business moves to DPT, announced Jan 15, 2026

geography.method: Regional revenue tagged in the filing's own XBRL instance: full-year contexts with one geographic dimension (or segments named after places), alone or crossed only with operating segments or a revenue line of the income statement; regions must add up to the revenue line within 1 percent; a member equal to the sum of others is a subtotal; the main split is the largest set of members adding up to the total; anything not broken out is a computed remainder.
